paper_title: Search for invisible axion dark matter with a multiple-cell haloscope
notes: CAPP-9T double-cell multiple-cell haloscope. Headline result (abstract + conclusion): excluded axions with g_agamma >= 11.1 x g_agamma^KSVZ at 90% CL over the mass range 13.0-13.9 ueV (3.14-3.36 GHz), rho_a=0.45 GeV/cm^3. Fig. 5 plots the exclusion in units of g_agamma/g_agamma^KSVZ (a nearly flat ~11.1 line with downward spikes to better sensitivity and gaps around 13.35 ueV from mode-mixing regions). Converted the flat 11.1x ratio to absolute g_agamma using KSVZ (E/N=0, |E/N-1.92|=1.92): g_agamma^KSVZ = alpha/(2*pi*f_a)*1.92 with f_a=5.7e6/m_a[eV] GeV (task-card mass convention m_a=5.7 ueV*(1e12 GeV/f_a)). This gives g_KSVZ ~ 5.1e-15 GeV^-1 at 13.0 ueV rising linearly with mass, so 11.1x = 5.6e-14 -> 6.0e-14 GeV^-1 across the band. Points trace the linear 11.1x envelope (the paper's headline/maximum limit); localized spikes below this and the 13.35 ueV gaps are not resolved here. data_source=text since the curve is reconstructed from the quoted 11.1x number rather than digitized point-by-point.
